root_cause.text: The radix_tree API fails to reclaim orphaned internal nodes when intermediate node allocations fail during tree construction, because radix_tree_for_each_slot() only visits slots containing leaf values and never traverses or frees unreferenced internal nodes.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "__radix_tree_create() allocates and links intermediate nodes into the tree one by one. If a subsequent allocation fails, the already-linked nodes remain in the tree with no corresponding leaf entry. These orphaned internal nodes are never reclaimed because radix_tree_for_each_slot() only visits slots containing leaf values." The patch resolves this by migrating from radix_tree to xarray, which "properly handles cleanup of internal nodes — xa_destroy() frees all internal xarray nodes when the qrtr_node is released, preventing the leak."

intent_record.intent_summary: Migrate from radix_tree to XArray API to simplify RCU locking and modernize the data structure implementation.

intent_record.how: The xa_load() function (XArray API) internally handles RCU locking for safe concurrent access to the tree structure, eliminating the need for explicit lock/unlock calls. This maintains thread-safety while simplifying the code path and reducing lock scope overhead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Migrate qrtr_tx_flow from deprecated radix tree API to modern XArray API for improved maintainability and consistency with current kernel standards.

intent_record.how: The XArray API provides a more modern interface for sparse array operations. xa_load() retrieves values similarly to radix_tree_lookup(), while xa_store() with GFP_KERNEL flag replaces the insert operation and returns an error code that xa_err() converts to a standard error value. This maintains the same functional behavior while using the updated kernel data structure API.
